y1: A father said to his two sons, 'Go and work in the vineyard today.' The older son said, 'I don't want to,' but later he changed his mind and went to work.
y2: The younger son said, 'Yes, I will go!' but he didn't go. Jesus asked, 'Which one did what his father wanted?' Actions that show obedience are more important than just words.
y4: A king prepared a wedding banquet for his son and called the guests. But the people who were invited went to their fields and businesses and didn't come.
y5: The king told his servants, 'Go out to the roads and invite anyone you see to the banquet.' So the wedding hall was filled with guests. God invites everyone.
y7: People asked Jesus a question to trick Him: 'Is it right to pay taxes to the Roman emperor or not?'
y8: Jesus looked at a coin and asked, 'Whose face is on this?' 'The emperor's.' 'Then give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give to God what belongs to God.' The people were amazed.
y10: A teacher of the law asked, 'Which commandment is the greatest?'
y11: Jesus answered, 'Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the first commandment. The second is like it: Love your neighbor as yourself.'
verse: “Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. … Love your neighbor as yourself.”
prayer: Dear God, thank You for inviting me to the banquet of the kingdom of heaven. Help me not just to say 'yes' with my words, but to obey with my actions. Let me love You with all my heart and love my neighbor as myself. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: obedience. Listening to what is said and doing it. The older son showed obedience later.
d1: wedding banquet. A big feast to celebrate a wedding. The king prepared a wedding banquet for his son.
d2: invite. To call someone to join you. God invites everyone.
d3: tax. Money paid to the government. Is it right to pay tax to the emperor?
d4: commandment. A rule or word God gives us to follow. The greatest commandment is love.
d5: neighbor. All the people around us. Love your neighbor as yourself.
